blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Senior feedback conversations carry a weight that junior ones rarely do. At the top of an organisation, the people who could tell an executive the uncomfortable truth are often the same people with the most to lose by doing so. Many choose, understandably, to stay quiet — and the executive receives, in consequence, the quietest truth in the building.

The remedy is not a harder tone. It is a carefully designed architecture of candour: a small number of trusted colleagues with standing permission to speak frankly, regular moments protected specifically for honest reflection, and a visible record of the feedback being acted on rather than merely received. Where those conditions exist, candid feedback flows without drama. Where they do not, it remains scarce regardless of how loudly it is requested.

On the receiving side, there is a parallel discipline. The executive who flinches visibly at uncomfortable feedback quietly teaches everyone around them never to do it again. The executive who thanks, pauses and acts — even slightly — teaches the opposite lesson. Each small moment either deposits into or withdraws from the trust account that determines how much truth the organisation dares to offer next time.

items.q: Why do the people best placed to tell an executive the truth often stay quiet?
options: They have never been asked for their view
They are the ones with the most to lose by speaking
They lack the vocabulary to phrase it
They doubt the executive can change
items.why: "the people who could tell an executive the uncomfortable truth are often the same people with the most to lose by doing so."

items.q: According to the text, what is the actual remedy for scarce candour?
options: Requesting feedback more loudly and more often
A deliberately designed architecture of candour
items.why: "The remedy is not a harder tone. It is a carefully designed architecture of candour."

items.q: What distinguishes feedback that is 'acted on' from feedback that is 'merely received'?
options: It is documented in the appraisal system
It is delivered by a consultant
It leaves a visible record of action
items.why: "a visible record of the feedback being acted on rather than merely received."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Silence at the top is often a rational choice for those below.
If leaders simply asked for candour more insistently, they would receive it.
How an executive reacts shapes what they will be told next time.
Trust between people behaves like an account with deposits and withdrawals.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a franqueza permanece escassa 'regardless of how loudly it is requested' — pedir mais alto não resolve.

items.q: The phrase "the quietest truth in the building" suggests that…
options: executives are told a softened, incomplete version of reality
the most important decisions are made in private
senior offices are physically quieter than open floors
truthful people speak in a low voice
items.why: Inferência: como os que sabem se calam, o executivo recebe a verdade mais amortecida e diluída da empresa.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie preparando um líder sênior para receber feedback difícil. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, in about twenty minutes, three of your peers are going to tell you things you would rather not hear. Before that, I want to talk about the first sixty seconds — because that is the part that actually matters.

Here is what I need you to understand. They have all rehearsed how you will react. Every one of them has, at some point, watched a senior leader flinch, and they have quietly filed it away. If you tense up, look away, or start explaining, you confirm the fear — and the next honest thing simply never gets said.

So we are going to keep it deliberately small. When each person finishes, you thank them. You pause — a real pause, not a rhetorical one. And then you say one specific thing you are going to do differently. Not a defence, not context, not a promise to reflect. One concrete action.

I know the instinct is to correct the record where you think they have it wrong. Resist it, at least today. You can revisit the facts next week. Today, the only thing you are building is the belief that it is safe to be honest with you. Get that right, and everything you hear for the next two years improves.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Which part of the conversation does Sophie say actually matters most?
options: The order in which the three peers speak
The first sixty seconds of his reaction
items.why: "I want to talk about the first sixty seconds — because that is the part that actually matters."

items.q: What exactly does Sophie want him to say after each person finishes?
options: A question asking them to elaborate
A promise to reflect and reply in writing
A thank-you, a real pause, and one specific action he will take
A short defence explaining the context
items.why: "you thank them. You pause… And then you say one specific thing you are going to do differently."

items.q: Why does Sophie tell him not to correct the facts today?
options: Because HR has forbidden any rebuttal
Because the peers will not remember the details
Because he can revisit them and the goal today is to make honesty feel safe
Because the facts are unimportant to his role
items.why: "You can revisit the facts next week. Today, the only thing you are building is the belief that it is safe to be honest with you."

items.q: When Sophie says "you confirm the fear," what fear does she mean?
options: The peers' fear of losing their jobs in a restructuring
The peers' fear that being honest with him is unsafe
The fear that the session will overrun
items.why: Inferência: a reação defensiva confirma o receio, latente nos colegas, de que ser franco com ele traz custo.

items.q: What can be inferred about why Sophie insists the pause be 'a real pause, not a rhetorical one'?
options: A long pause makes the meeting run late
A performed pause reads as insincere and undoes the effect
He tends to interrupt people when nervous
Silence is required by the feedback policy
items.why: Inferência: uma pausa encenada é percebida como técnica vazia; só a pausa genuína sinaliza que ele de fato absorveu o que ouviu.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her candour in that review was rare — she named the real problem while everyone else hedged." Candour is…
items.why: Candour = franqueza: dizer a verdade sem rodeios nem verniz.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every unmet promise makes a small withdrawal from the ___ that keeps the team open with you."
items.why: Trust account = conta de confiança: cada gesto deposita ou saca desse saldo relacional.

items.q: "The moment he flinched, the room went quiet and the honesty stopped." To flinch is to…
items.why: To flinch = estremecer/recuar: uma reação involuntária que revela desconforto.

items.q: Organisational silence is best described as…
options: a formal quiet-hours policy in the office
the collective withholding of things people know but dare not say
items.why: É o silêncio coletivo: as pessoas sabem, mas se calam por medo do custo de falar.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "A senior mentor with ___ can challenge you at any time, without asking leave each time."
items.why: Standing permission = permissão permanente: o direito, já concedido, de falar francamente quando quiser.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de feedback sênior. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When feedback stings, most leaders instinctively push back." To push back means to…
items.why: Push back = resistir, contestar — a reação defensiva que Sophie pede que ele evite.

items.q: "He thanked them, then actually followed through on the change." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — o oposto de só 'refletir'.

items.q: "Thanking people while ignoring their input rings hollow." It…
items.why: Ring hollow = soar vazio/falso, sem substância por trás.

items.q: "One defensive reply can shut down a candid conversation for good." To shut down means to…
items.why: Shut down = interromper de vez, encerrar bruscamente a abertura.

items.q: "A single honest exchange rarely moves the needle — the architecture does." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
